artifact.reason: Existing Docker Compose configuration that needs modification to add web service. Contains networking configuration (annie-network), health checks patterns, and environment variable setup to follow.

artifact.symbol: FastAPI app, CORS middleware, health endpoints
artifact.reason: Shows FastAPI application structure including CORS configuration that web UI will need to work with. Health endpoints pattern for reference.
Chat endpoint that web UI will call. Request/response models define the API contract for sending messages.
SSE streaming endpoint that web UI will connect to for real-time responses. Defines event types: status, token, tool_call, tool_result, done, error.

constraints.constraint: New `web/` directory at project root alongside `backend/`, `mcp_server/`, `telegram_bot/`
Docker service name: `web` (maps to port 3000 in dev, 80 in prod via nginx)
Must connect to annie-network for backend API access
Depends on: `backend` service for API proxying
Use Vite ^5.0.0 with React 18 and TypeScript 5.3+
No strict performance targets - Annie is a thinking machine. Focus on functionality.
Multi-stage Dockerfile: node:20-alpine for build, nginx:alpine for production
Follow existing Docker Compose patterns: health checks, restart policies, volume mounts, environment variables
Follow existing project structure conventions for consistency

interface.name: POST /api/chat
interface.signature: POST /api/chat { user_id: string, platform: string, message: string, context?: object, files?: FileAttachment[] } => { conversation_id: string, status: string, stream_url: string, timestamp: string }

interface.name: GET /api/stream/{conversation_id}
interface.signature: GET /api/stream/{conversation_id} => EventSource(status | token | tool_call | tool_result | done | error)

interface.name: GET /health/full
interface.signature: GET /health/full => { status: string, components: { mcp_server, redis, llm_api, agentic_memories, langfuse }, timestamp: string }

tests.standards: The Annie project uses pytest for backend testing. For the web frontend, no testing framework is specified yet. Story 20.1 focuses on project setup and infrastructure - actual UI testing comes in later stories (Story 20.15). The main testing for this story is verification via Docker build success and manual checks.
